claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent more than a hundred thousand years getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: Mitalas & Sills 1992, ApJ 401, 759 (NASA ADS scan, both pages read); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17); NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17 with the supplied CA bundle); Crossref record for Stix 2003 (paper itself not reachable)
claims.note: The quotes in SOURCES are accurate: M&S give t_d = 1.7e5 yr (centre to the base of the convection zone) and call 3e3-3e4 yr 'much too short'; MSFC says an individual photon takes 'about a million years' to reach the interface layer. But a cited NASA source, SVS, says 40,000 years to the surface, which is below the hook's floor. The 'energy, not one photon' framing does not avoid this: the 1e5 floor comes from M&S, which is also a photon diffusion time. A3 asks for the narrower claim the best source supports, and the narrower claim here is 'tens of thousands of years or more', which M&S, MSFC and SVS all support. 'More than 100,000' picks the higher floor. My own reading also raises doubt about the 1.7e5 itself. This is not a source: M&S eq. 2 uses 3<r^2> = N<l^2>, whereas for a 3-D random flight <R^2> = N<l^2>. That would make the result about 3x too long, giving roughly 6e4 yr, in line with SVS. Also, the Sun's radiation energy content divided by its luminosity, using MSFC's temperatures, is of order 1e4 yr. Stix's ~3e7 yr was not read at source (Crossref only: Solar Physics 212, 3-6, 2003). Change the hook to a claim every cited source supports, e.g. 'spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out of the Sun', and change the 100,000+ tags and the title to match; or, if the owner wants to keep 100,000+, stop and ask (F4) and find an A2 source that refutes the SVS 40,000 figure. Also drop the SOURCES line 'the published answers run higher, never lower': SVS (40,000) and the 3e3-3e4 yr textbook values M&S quote both run lower.

claims.claim: First ~2 s (A4): 'The energy in the sunlight on your skin' over the Sun-Earth shot, a bright pulse crossing the gap, Earth labelled 'not to scale'.
claims.source_checked: Alignment JSON (words to 'skin' end at ~2.3 s; pulse runs frames 6-106) and index.tsx; NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17 with the supplied CA bundle)
claims.note: By second 2 nothing has been asserted beyond the light crossing from the Sun to Earth, which SVS states, and the shot is labelled not to scale. A swipe after the full first sentence (5.5 s) carries claim 1's problem, so it is covered there. The hook says 'energy', not 'the light is 100,000 years old', which avoids the popular myth.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: NIST CODATA c = 299 792 458 m/s exact (physics.nist.gov); NSSDC Earth fact sheet (semimajor axis 149.598e6 km, perihelion 147.095, aphelion 152.100); NSSDC Sun fact sheet (149.6e6 km mean); NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17 with the supplied CA bundle); IAU 2012 B2 not reachable (iau.org returned 404)
claims.note: SVS says verbatim: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth'. Computed: 8.18-8.46 min over the year, so 'eight minutes' is fair rounding. A SOURCES nit that does not affect the verdict: 1 AU/c = 499 s is centre to centre. Photosphere to Earth is ~497 s (8 min 17 s), not '8 min 19 s from the photosphere'. Tidy this, and cite NSSDC or SVS next to the IAU 2012 resolution, since the IAU page was not reachable here.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.source_checked: Mitalas & Sills 1992, ApJ 401, 759 (NASA ADS scan, both pages read); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17); NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17 with the supplied CA bundle)
claims.note: Eight minutes against 4e4 yr (SVS), 1.7e5 yr (M&S) or ~1e6 yr (MSFC). True under every cited figure, and still true after the claim 1 fix.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17); NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17 with the supplied CA bundle)
claims.note: MSFC: inside, the radiation is 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays', the outer 30% is crossed by 'convective fluid flows', and the energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. SVS: each photon is 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly'. Both support 'not the same light'.

claims.claim: Deep inside, it travels mostly as gamma rays and X-rays.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17)
claims.note: This is MSFC's own wording: 'This energy diffuses outward by radiation (mostly gamma-rays and x-rays) through the radiative zone'. A3 is met. Caveat carried in SOURCES 4: thermal radiation at 2-15 MK is overwhelmingly X-rays, and the captions highlight 'gamma rays'. 'mostly X-rays' would be the safer physics wording, but the cited source does support the line as spoken.

claims.claim: It leaves as sunlight.

claims.note: MSFC: the reactions 'release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'.

claims.note: Qualitative. 'Ancient' holds at every cited figure (4e4 yr and up), so it survives the claim 1 fix.

claims.claim: Its last eight minutes were the trip to you.
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17 with the supplied CA bundle); NIST c; NSSDC Earth fact sheet
claims.note: Same basis as claim 3 (SVS: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel ... from the sun to Earth').

claims.claim: Sun-Earth shot (start and end): Earth labelled 'not to scale' while visible; a bright pulse crosses the gap.

claims.note: A6 is met: the label sits under Earth for as long as Earth is visible. The drawing is ~24x too big and ~39x too close (Sun r 110 vs Earth r 24; gap of 5.5 R_sun vs 215), and that is what the label discloses. The pulse is only a depiction of the light's trip, which claim 3 confirms.

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES / surface to your skin / not to scale
claims.source_checked: Same as claim 3
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth is 8.2-8.5 min over the year. The tag carries a 'not to scale' label.

claims.claim: 100,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not to scale
claims.source_checked: Same as claim 1
claims.note: Same problem as claim 1: SVS gives 40,000 yr to the surface. 'Core to surface' is otherwise consistent, since M&S's 1.7e5 runs centre to 0.71 R and convection only adds time. Change it to whatever claim 1 becomes (e.g. '10,000s OF YEARS+' or 'TENS OF THOUSANDS OF YEARS').

claims.claim: THE ENERGY / 100,000+ years getting out
claims.source_checked: Same as claim 1
claims.note: Same as claims 1 and 12. Make it match the revised hook. The title in index.tsx ('The energy in sunlight took 100,000+ years to get out of the Sun') needs the same change (E2).

claims.claim: THE TRIP / 8 minutes to you / not to scale
claims.source_checked: Same as claim 3
claims.note: As claim 3.

claims.claim: Cutaway rings at 0.25 and 0.7 of the Sun's radius (core / radiative zone / convection zone).
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17)
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%' (175,000 km), the radiative zone runs 'from 25% ... to 70%', and convection is 'the outermost 30%'. The 0.713 R helioseismic depth in SOURCES (Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991) was checked on Crossref only (ApJ 378, 413, title 'The depth of the solar convection zone'). The figure itself was not re-read, but the visual uses MSFC's 0.7.

claims.claim: Random-walk path from the centre to the 0.7 ring, not entering the convection zone; tag on screen says 'not to scale'.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17); NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (fetched 2026-11-17 with the supplied CA bundle); Mitalas & Sills 1992, ApJ 401, 759 (NASA ADS scan, both pages read); index.tsx WALK
claims.note: MSFC: photons 'bounce from particle to particle through the radiative zone'. SVS describes a 'drunken walk'. M&S time the walk from the centre to the base of the convection zone. The code scales the walk so it never exceeds 0.7, then exits at 0.7. A schematic walk of ~240 steps, disclosed by the 'not to scale' sub-label on the 100,000+ tag, which is up for the whole cutaway. Nit: SOURCES 6 says the walk is 'through the radiative zone', but it starts at r = 0 in the core. That matches M&S's centre-to-0.71 R timing, so it is fine; the wording in SOURCES could say so.

claims.claim: Path colour from violet toward pale yellow by log temperature (15 MK at r=0, 7 MK at 0.25 R, 2 MK at 0.7 R, 5,700 K at the surface; ~10% of the way at 0.25 R, ~26% at 0.7 R).
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched 2026-11-17); index.tsx PROFILE/tint
claims.note: MSFC: centre 'about 15,000,000 C', radiative zone '7,000,000 C to about 2,000,000 C', surface '5,700 K'. At MK, the gap between C and K is negligible. Recomputed: ln(15/7)/ln(15e6/5700) = 9.7% and ln(7.5)/ln(15e6/5700) = 25.6%, matching the code and SOURCES 6. The hue mapping is schematic and carries no on-screen label, so it asserts no specific wavelength.
